newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower as wheat falls, technicals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower as wheat falls, technicals.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on a sharp drop in wheat futures and on technical selling, traders said.
Corn was firm early on outlooks for frost early next week in portions of the northern U.S. Midwest.
But bullish momentum waned as spot September, which expired at 1201 CDT, faltered early and technical sell orders just under resistance at $3.20 in the December knocked the market lower.
The session high for December was $3.19.
Refco Inc sold 3.5 million bushels of December, Merrill Lynch Futuers sold two million December and Tenco Inc sold two million December, they said.
Cargill Inc bought seven million bushels of December, the traders said.
Corn was underpinned by firm cash basis markets amid slow farmer selling, they said.
Corn closed 3/4 to 3-1/4 cents a bushel lower. September expired at 1201 CDT, down 3/4 cent at $3.54-3/4. December closed two cents lower at $3.13-1/2.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 55,000 contracts, down from 69,664 Wednesday, according to the CBOT.

In corn options, Smith Barney sold 1,000 December 1997 puts at 14 cents, Cargill Investor Services bought 450 December $3.50 calls at 3-1/4 cents, Refco Inc bought 400 December $3.50 calls at 3-3/8 and Refco bought 400 December $3.40 calls at five cents, traders said. Refco also bought 400 December $3.30 calls at 7-1/2 cents, sources said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 22,000 contracts, down from 32,091 Wednesday.
